correctness.rationale: A unique stationary random series follows from a uniform 1/3 contraction. Its support is [0,1] because adding [0,1/3] bridges every complementary gap of (2/3) times the standard Cantor set. Centering and regrouping independent fair ternary digits gives the exact m-multiplicity product. Adjacent factors yield a uniform power-Fourier exponent log_3(16/9)>1/2 and hence L2 plus a positive H^s range. At t_N=(pi/2)3^(N+1) its modulus is exactly B A^N, with A>4/9>1/3, so t_N times the modulus diverges; the finite distributional derivative of a BV density would contradict this. Uniform lower bounds on fixed-size resonance bands give the upper Sobolev exclusion. Finite product calculations are reproducibility checks only.

value.rationale: The fair ternary Cantor driver and same contraction 1/3 are an intrinsic resonant point of the classical second-generation uncountable affine IFS. The finding separates full interval support and a genuine L2 invariant density from bounded-variation regularity, which is a central diagnostic in the earlier invariant-measure literature. The exact Fourier lattice and two one-sided Sobolev bounds make the distinction quantitatively testable and reveal a specific arithmetic obstruction, rather than an arbitrary isolated parameter computation.
